properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] Dev/CI Toolchain Credential Read + Egress to Non-Canonical Registry
properties.description:
Detects a developer/CI toolchain process (node, npm, npx, yarn, pnpm, cosign, skopeo, docker, oras) reading or writing a registry-credential file (~/.docker/config.json, ~/.config/containers/auth.json, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials) and, within a five-minute window on the same host, opening a TLS/registry connection to an OCI/artifact registry that is NOT on the canonical-registry allowlist. This fortnight it is driven by CVE-2026-59891 ("Credential confusion in @sigstore/oci can leak registry credentials to an attacker-controlled registry"), where getRegistryCredentials() substring-matches Docker auth keys and hands credentials to a lookalike registry host, and by the broader dev-supply-chain exposure theme in "The Attacker Never Sleeps, Neither Can Your Testing," "The Generator Can't Be the Validator (OpenAI/Hugging Face)" and the Gitea token-scope bypass CVE-2026-58443. It spans the credential-access and exfiltration kill-chain stages: read secret material from disk, then ship it (or authenticate with it) to attacker infrastructure over an alternative protocol. It FIRES when a build/attestation tool touches a credential store and then egresses to a registry host outside the maintained canonical set (private ECR/GCR/GHCR/Harbor/Nexus/Artifactory endpoints that don't match your allowlist land here as first-seen). It does NOT fire on normal pushes/pulls to canonical registries (docker.io, ghcr.io, registry.npmjs.org, gcr.io, quay.io, *.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com allowlisted, mcr.microsoft.com), nor on a credential read with no subsequent non-canonical egress inside the window.

Rationale: Every article in scope converges on dev/CI trust abuse; the sharpest shared, multi-platform-detectable signal is the CVE-2026-59891 chain of a build tool reading a registry-credential store then egressing to a registry host outside the canonical set — a technique-level pattern that survives IOC rotation because it keys on tool+cred-file+non-canonical-destination, not on any specific attacker registry.
properties.query:
let CanonicalReg = dynamic(["ghcr.io","docker.io","index.docker.io","registry-1.docker.io","registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","gcr.io","quay.io","registry.k8s.io","mcr.microsoft.com","public.ecr.aws"]);
let CredWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("config.json","auth.json",".npmrc","credentials")
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\.docker", "/.docker", @"\.aws", "/.aws", ".config/containers", ".npmrc")
    | project CredTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, CredFile = FolderPath, CredUser = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 5000)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","cosign.exe","skopeo","docker.exe","oras.exe")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(registry|ghcr|\.cr\.|dkr\.ecr|azurecr|pkg\.dev|harbor|nexus|artifactory)"
| where not(RemoteUrl in~ (CanonicalReg))
| join kind=inner CredWrites on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (CredTime .. CredTime + 5m)
| project CredTime, EgressTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, CredTime),
          DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          RemoteUrl, CredFile, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by EgressTime desc
